title: Picture, scene and story lessons
summary: Drills built on drawings: a picture per word, one illustrated scene, or a story told in panels.
description: Lessons built on drawings, for what is learnt faster from a picture than from a translation. The drawings are made by an image model and kept.

stories.want: to learn them from pictures instead of translations
stories.soThat: the word attaches to the thing

requirements.text: In a picture lesson each word is drawn once and the drawing is kept; the learner sees the picture and picks the word, and sees the word and picks the picture.
A word's picture is stored as a JPEG at most `picture.word-side` on a side.
A scene lesson has 6 to 10 things in one picture and at most 6 sentences saying where something is.
Where a thing is in a scene uses only the prepositions in `scene.prepositions`.
After a scene is drawn, a vision model locates each thing in it; a scene is ready only when at least 5 things are found.
A story lesson has 4 to 8 panels, 1 to 3 sentences under each picture and 1 to 4 characters.
A drawing that was not finished when the app closed is resumed the next time it starts, by the device that started it.
A scene or story whose drawing failed says so on its page and can be tried again; a picture lesson offers to draw the pictures still missing.

values.description: The longest side of a word's stored picture.
The prepositions a scene's sentences use to say where something is.
